effect: Severe risk of major bleeding and gastrointestinal hemorrhage due to combined anticoagulant and antiplatelet effects.
recommendation: Avoid combination unless strictly indicated for mechanical heart valves with careful INR monitoring.

effect: Contrast-induced nephropathy leading to severe metformin accumulation and fatal lactic acidosis.
recommendation: Withhold metformin 48 hours prior to contrast imaging and resume 48 hours post-procedure after checking serum creatinine.

effect: Potentiation of nitric oxide-cGMP pathway causing profound, refractory hypotension and myocardial infarction.
recommendation: Strictly contraindicated. Do not co-prescribe within 24 hours of each other.

effect: NSAIDs decrease renal clearance of methotrexate, causing severe bone marrow suppression and hepatotoxicity.
recommendation: Avoid co-administration; use paracetamol for analgesia if necessary.

effect: CYP3A4 inhibition increases statin systemic exposure, drastically raising rhabdomyolysis and acute renal failure risk.
recommendation: Temporarily suspend atorvastatin during macrolide antibiotic therapy or switch to rosuvastatin/azithromycin.

effect: Inhibition of theophylline metabolism leads to theophylline toxicity, tachycardia, seizures, and arrhythmias.
recommendation: Monitor theophylline levels and reduce dose by 50% or choose alternative antibiotic.

effect: Enhanced serotonergic activity leading to life-threatening Serotonin Syndrome and reduced seizure threshold.
recommendation: Avoid combination; monitor for tremor, hyperthermia, agitation, and clonus.

effect: P-glycoprotein inhibition causes 70% increase in serum digoxin concentration, inducing fatal digitalis arrhythmias.
recommendation: Reduce digoxin dosage by 50% upon starting amiodarone and monitor digoxin serum levels.

effect: Combined potassium-sparing effect leads to severe hyperkalemia and cardiac arrest risk, especially in renal impairment.
recommendation: Check baseline serum potassium and creatinine; monitor weekly initially.

effect: CYP2C19 competitive inhibition reduces clopidogrel active metabolite formation, decreasing antiplatelet efficacy.
recommendation: Use pantoprazole or famotidine instead of omeprazole.

effect: Insoluble chelate formation in GI tract reduces levothyroxine bioavailability.
recommendation: Space administration by at least 4 hours.

effect: Divalent and trivalent cations chelate fluoroquinolones, drastically impairing gut absorption.
recommendation: Administer ciprofloxacin 2 hours before or 6 hours after antacids.

effect: Dual antithrombotic effect markedly increases major and intracranial bleeding risk.
recommendation: Reserve for high-risk indications with gastroprotection and the shortest feasible duration.

effect: NSAID platelet inhibition plus gastric erosion amplifies anticoagulant bleeding risk.
recommendation: Avoid; use paracetamol. If unavoidable, add a PPI and monitor INR closely.

effect: Additive antiplatelet and mucosal injury effects raise GI bleeding risk several-fold.
recommendation: Avoid NSAIDs in warfarin patients; prefer paracetamol or topical NSAIDs.

effect: CYP2C9 inhibition sharply reduces warfarin metabolism, causing supratherapeutic INR and hemorrhage.
recommendation: Reduce warfarin dose by 25-50% and check INR within 3-5 days of starting fluconazole.

effect: CYP2C9/3A4 and P-gp inhibition can double the anticoagulant effect, precipitating fatal bleeding.
recommendation: Reduce warfarin dose by 30-50% when amiodarone is started; monitor INR weekly for a month.

effect: CYP2C9 inhibition elevates S-warfarin levels, causing dangerous INR elevation.
recommendation: Halve the warfarin dose and monitor INR on day 4-5 of therapy.

effect: Fluoroquinolone inhibition of warfarin metabolism plus gut flora suppression raises INR and bleeding risk.
recommendation: Monitor INR at baseline and 3-5 days after starting; adjust dose as needed.

effect: Biphasic CYP interaction initially raises then lowers INR; protein-binding displacement adds volatility.
recommendation: Monitor INR and phenytoin levels closely; anticipate dose changes in both directions.

effect: Potent CYP3A4/2C9 induction can reduce warfarin effect by more than half, risking thrombosis.
recommendation: Increase warfarin dose empirically with frequent INR monitoring; re-reduce after rifampin stops.

effect: Strong CYP2C9 inhibition plus antiplatelet action causes severe hemorrhagic risk.
recommendation: Contraindicated combination; choose an alternative analgesic.

effect: Parenteral high-potency NSAID with anticoagulant produces a high rate of major GI and surgical bleeding.
recommendation: Avoid in anticoagulated patients; use paracetamol or opioids instead.

effect: Androgen-mediated reduction of clotting factor synthesis potentiates anticoagulation unpredictably.
recommendation: Monitor INR frequently and reduce warfarin dose empirically when danazol is added.

effect: Fluoropyrimidines inhibit warfarin metabolism, causing marked INR elevation and bleeding.
recommendation: Monitor INR at least twice weekly during chemotherapy and reduce warfarin dose.

effect: Capecitabine (a 5-FU prodrug) inhibits CYP2C9, elevating INR and bleeding risk.
recommendation: Monitor INR closely during treatment; empiric warfarin dose reduction is often required.

effect: Disulfiram inhibits warfarin metabolism, producing unexpected over-anticoagulation.
recommendation: Check INR 3-5 days after starting disulfiram and reduce warfarin dose proactively.

effect: Antiandrogen inhibits warfarin clearance, causing dangerous INR elevation.
recommendation: Monitor INR weekly during initiation and reduce warfarin dose by 25-50%.

effect: Even topical or oral azole therapy can markedly inhibit warfarin metabolism and cause bleeding.
recommendation: Prefer topical route only; monitor INR if any azole antifungal is used.

effect: Combined anticoagulants with no monitoring marker substantially raise major and intracranial bleeding risk.
recommendation: Contraindicated in routine practice; only under specialist supervision.

effect: Uricosuric displaces warfarin from albumin and inhibits its metabolism, amplifying effect.
recommendation: Avoid; if used, reduce warfarin dose and monitor INR daily initially.

effect: Trimethoprim inhibits warfarin metabolism, raising INR and bleeding risk.
recommendation: Monitor INR closely during TMP-SMX and reduce warfarin dose.

effect: Overlapping anticoagulation increases hemorrhage risk without a reliable monitoring marker.
recommendation: Avoid routine combination; specialist decision only.

effect: Azithromycin can raise INR and bleeding risk in susceptible patients.
recommendation: Check INR 3-5 days after starting azithromycin.

effect: Terbinafine inhibits warfarin metabolism, raising INR.
recommendation: Monitor INR during oral terbinafine therapy.

effect: SSRI platelet-serotonin depletion plus CYP effects raise bleeding risk.
recommendation: Monitor INR and clinical bleeding; consider gastroprotection.

effect: SSRIs increase bleeding risk through platelet inhibition and possible INR changes.
recommendation: Monitor INR and watch for bruising or GI bleeding.

effect: Atorvastatin can modestly raise INR via CYP interactions.
recommendation: Monitor INR after starting atorvastatin.

effect: Strong CYP3A4/P-gp inhibition raises rivaroxaban levels, increasing major bleeding risk.
recommendation: Avoid dual therapy; if required, cap at 15 mg and monitor for bleeding.

effect: Ritonavir roughly doubles apixaban exposure and bleeding risk.
recommendation: Avoid; if required, halve the apixaban dose and monitor closely.

effect: P-gp inhibition increases dabigatran exposure, raising bleeding risk.
recommendation: Consider dose reduction in elderly/renal impairment; monitor for bleeding.

effect: Combined anticoagulant and antiplatelet effects raise major bleeding risk.
recommendation: Use with caution, lowest effective doses, and clinical monitoring.

effect: MAOI plus SSRI precipitates serotonin syndrome with hyperthermia and death risk.
recommendation: Contraindicated. Observe a 14-day washout in either direction.

effect: MAOI blocks dextromethorphan metabolism, causing severe serotonin syndrome.
recommendation: Avoid all OTC cough preparations containing dextromethorphan during MAOI therapy.

effect: Even transdermal selegiline plus SSRI can trigger serotonin syndrome.
recommendation: Use only with documented tolerance at low doses; otherwise wash out 14 days.

effect: Reversible MAO inhibition by linezolid plus SSRI raises serotonin syndrome risk.
recommendation: Monitor closely for serotonin toxicity; consider alternative antibiotic.

effect: SNRI plus MAO-inhibiting oxazolidinone increases serotonin syndrome risk.
recommendation: Monitor BP and serotonin-toxicity signs; prefer alternative antimicrobial.

effect: Methylene blue is a potent MAO inhibitor that precipitates serotonin syndrome with SSRIs.
recommendation: Contraindicated. Stop SSRI 2 weeks before elective methylene-blue use.

effect: MAOI plus serotonergic opioid causes serotonin syndrome and lowers seizure threshold.
recommendation: Avoid; substitute a non-serotonergic analgesic.

effect: Classic MAOI-opioid interaction causing serotonin syndrome and hyperthermia.
recommendation: Contraindicated; meperidine must never be used with any MAO inhibitor.

effect: Reversible MAO-A inhibitor plus SSRI raises serotonin syndrome risk.
recommendation: Observe a washout period and avoid the combination.

effect: SSRI plus serotonergic opioid raises serotonin syndrome and seizure risk.
recommendation: Monitor for agitation, tremor, or clonus; consider alternative analgesic.

effect: Serotonergic OTC antitussive plus SSRI can precipitate serotonin syndrome.
recommendation: Advise patients to avoid dextromethorphan-containing products.

effect: CYP1A2 inhibition multiplies tizanidine exposure, causing profound hypotension and sedation.
recommendation: Contraindicated; use an alternative muscle relaxant or SSRI.

effect: CYP1A2 inhibition by ciprofloxacin raises tizanidine levels, causing severe hypotension and bradycardia.
recommendation: Contraindicated; avoid tizanidine during fluoroquinolone therapy.

effect: CYP1A2 inhibition can triple clozapine levels, causing seizures and severe sedation.
recommendation: Avoid; if unavoidable, reduce clozapine by 50% and monitor levels.

effect: Caffeine inhibits CYP1A2, raising clozapine levels unpredictably.
recommendation: Advise consistent caffeine intake and monitor clozapine levels.

effect: Additive antifolate effect causes severe pancytopenia and fatal myelosuppression.
recommendation: Contraindicated. Use an alternative antibiotic such as a cephalosporin.

effect: Penicillins reduce renal tubular secretion of methotrexate, delaying clearance and worsening toxicity.
recommendation: Monitor CBC and methotrexate levels closely; consider dose reduction.

effect: Cisplatin impairs renal methotrexate excretion, causing profound pancytopenia and mucositis.
recommendation: Sequence carefully with hydration, leucovorin rescue, and level monitoring.

effect: NSAID-induced reduction in renal methotrexate clearance leads to severe myelosuppression.
recommendation: Avoid NSAIDs during high-dose methotrexate; use paracetamol.

effect: Strong CYP3A4 inhibition multiplies statin exposure, causing rhabdomyolysis and acute kidney injury.
recommendation: Withhold simvastatin during azole therapy; switch to pravastatin/rosuvastatin.

effect: Macrolide CYP3A4 inhibition greatly increases simvastatin levels, risking rhabdomyolysis.
recommendation: Stop simvastatin for the antibiotic course or switch to azithromycin.

effect: CYP3A4 inhibition raises simvastatin exposure, increasing myopathy risk.
recommendation: Cap simvastatin at 20 mg daily with diltiazem; monitor for muscle pain.

effect: Amiodarone raises simvastatin levels, increasing myopathy and rhabdomyolysis risk.
recommendation: Cap simvastatin at 20 mg daily and monitor for muscle symptoms.

effect: Amlodipine increases simvastatin exposure, raising myopathy risk.
recommendation: Cap simvastatin at 20 mg daily when co-prescribed with amlodipine.

effect: Verapamil inhibits CYP3A4, increasing lovastatin levels and myopathy risk.
recommendation: Limit lovastatin to 20 mg daily or switch to pravastatin/rosuvastatin.

effect: Fibrate-statin combination increases the risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis.
recommendation: Use lowest effective statin dose; monitor for muscle pain or dark urine.

effect: Gemfibrozil displaces warfarin and inhibits its metabolism, raising INR.
recommendation: Monitor INR closely when gemfibrozil is added.

effect: NSAIDs reduce renal lithium clearance, causing lithium toxicity with tremor, ataxia, and seizures.
recommendation: Avoid NSAIDs; use paracetamol. Monitor lithium levels 3-5 days after any NSAID start.

effect: ACE inhibitors reduce lithium clearance and can precipitate life-threatening lithium toxicity.
recommendation: Monitor lithium levels weekly during initiation and after dose changes.

effect: Thiazide-induced sodium depletion increases renal lithium reabsorption, causing toxicity.
recommendation: Reduce lithium dose by 25-50% when a thiazide is started; monitor levels.

effect: ARBs reduce renal lithium excretion, raising serum levels toward the toxic range.
recommendation: Monitor lithium levels 1-2 weeks after starting or changing the ARB.

effect: Metronidazole reduces lithium clearance, precipitating lithium intoxication.
recommendation: Monitor lithium levels during and 3-5 days after metronidazole therapy.

effect: COX-2 inhibition can raise lithium levels, though less than traditional NSAIDs.
recommendation: Monitor lithium levels when celecoxib is added.

effect: P-gp inhibition plus additive AV-node suppression raises digoxin levels and causes bradyarrhythmia.
recommendation: Reduce digoxin dose by 40-50% and monitor levels, heart rate, and ECG.

effect: Macrolide P-gp inhibition acutely elevates digoxin concentration, causing toxicity.
recommendation: Halve digoxin dose when starting clarithromycin; monitor levels within a week.

effect: Azithromycin can raise digoxin levels via P-gp inhibition, precipitating arrhythmia.
recommendation: Monitor digoxin levels; watch for nausea, visual changes, and bradycardia.

effect: Dronedarone increases digoxin levels several-fold via P-gp inhibition.
recommendation: Halve the digoxin dose when starting dronedarone; monitor levels and rhythm.

effect: Metoclopramide increases GI motility and P-gp effects, reducing digoxin absorption.
recommendation: Monitor digoxin levels when metoclopramide is started or stopped.

effect: Loop-diuretic-induced hypokalemia potentiates digoxin toxicity.
recommendation: Monitor potassium and digoxin levels; supplement potassium as needed.

effect: CYP3A4/P-gp inhibition can multiply colchicine levels, causing fatal neuromuscular and multiorgan toxicity.
recommendation: Contraindicated, especially with renal impairment; use alternative antibiotic.

effect: Macrolide inhibition of colchicine metabolism causes severe, often fatal colchicine toxicity.
recommendation: Avoid combination; if unavoidable, use lowest dose with close monitoring.

effect: Fusidic acid inhibits colchicine clearance, raising the risk of severe toxicity.
recommendation: Avoid concurrent use; choose an alternative antimicrobial.

effect: CYP3A4/P-gp inhibition raises colchicine levels, increasing toxicity risk.
recommendation: Use lowest colchicine dose; monitor for muscle weakness or GI toxicity.

effect: CYP3A4 inhibition raises tacrolimus levels, causing nephrotoxicity and neurotoxicity.
recommendation: Monitor tacrolimus trough levels daily during macrolide therapy.

effect: Macrolide CYP3A4 inhibition increases cyclosporine exposure, risking acute renal failure.
recommendation: Monitor cyclosporine troughs and creatinine at least twice weekly.

effect: Strong CYP3A4 inhibition multiplies sirolimus levels, causing toxicity.
recommendation: Avoid; if unavoidable, reduce sirolimus by ~80% and monitor troughs.

effect: Strong CYP3A4 inhibition multiplies sirolimus levels, causing toxicity.
recommendation: Avoid; if unavoidable, reduce sirolimus by ~80% and monitor troughs.

effect: Strong CYP3A4 inhibition raises eplerenone levels, causing severe hyperkalemia.
recommendation: Contraindicated; do not combine with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors.

effect: CYP3A4 inhibition increases imatinib plasma levels, causing edema, cytopenia, and hepatotoxicity.
recommendation: Avoid co-administration; monitor for imatinib toxicity if required.

effect: Thiazide-induced hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia potentiate sotalol QT effect.
recommendation: Correct electrolytes proactively and monitor ECG.

effect: Both prolong QT; combined use markedly raises torsades de pointes risk.
recommendation: Monitor ECG and electrolytes; reduce doses or use less QT-prolonging agent.

effect: Additive QT prolongation from two antiemetic agents.
recommendation: Avoid combining two QT-prolonging antiemetics; monitor ECG if unavoidable.

effect: Additive QT prolongation from macrolide plus class III antiarrhythmic.
recommendation: Prefer a non-QT antibiotic; monitor ECG if combination required.

effect: CYP3A4 inhibition plus additive QT effects raise the risk of torsades de pointes.
recommendation: Avoid combination; use an alternative prokinetic or antibiotic.

effect: Azole inhibition raises pimozide levels, causing severe QT prolongation and torsades.
recommendation: Contraindicated; use a non-interacting antifungal or antipsychotic.

effect: Amiodarone raises flecainide levels, risking proarrhythmia and QRS widening.
recommendation: Reduce flecainide dose by 30-50%; monitor ECG for QRS prolongation.

effect: Combined AV-node suppression causes severe bradycardia, hypotension, and heart block.
recommendation: Use lower doses with ECG monitoring; avoid in conduction disease.

effect: Additive negative chronotropy and inotropy can precipitate symptomatic bradycardia.
recommendation: Monitor ECG and blood pressure; reduce doses of both agents.

effect: Additive sinus-node suppression causes severe bradycardia and heart block.
recommendation: Contraindicated; do not combine with non-dihydropyridine CCBs.

effect: Benzodiazepine plus opioid causes synergistic respiratory depression, coma, and death.
recommendation: Avoid unless no alternative; lowest doses, monitor respirations, co-prescribe naloxone.

effect: Z-drug plus opioid markedly increases respiratory depression and overdose risk.
recommendation: Avoid; if unavoidable, reduce both doses and monitor respiratory rate.

effect: Barbiturate induction lowers methadone levels, precipitating withdrawal and relapse.
recommendation: Monitor for withdrawal and titrate methadone dose; avoid abrupt changes.

effect: Potent enzyme induction reduces methadone levels, causing withdrawal.
recommendation: Expect a large dose increase; monitor for withdrawal and re-taper after rifampin stops.

effect: Azole inhibition of CYP3A4 causes prolonged sedation and respiratory depression.
recommendation: Avoid oral midazolam with azoles; monitor sedation and respiratory rate.

effect: Ritonavir can increase triazolam exposure many-fold, causing profound CNS depression.
recommendation: Contraindicated; use a non-benzodiazepine alternative.

effect: CYP3A4 inhibition raises buspirone levels, causing dizziness and sedation.
recommendation: Limit buspirone to 10 mg total daily dose and monitor for toxicity.

effect: Enzyme induction accelerates estrogen/progestogen metabolism, causing contraceptive failure.
recommendation: Use a non-hormonal or high-dose method during and 4 weeks after rifampin.

effect: CYP3A4 induction reduces contraceptive steroid levels, risking unintended pregnancy.
recommendation: Use a higher-dose or non-hormonal contraceptive; counsel on breakthrough bleeding.

effect: Macrolide inhibition raises carbamazepine levels, producing ataxia, diplopia, and toxicity.
recommendation: Monitor carbamazepine levels; consider azithromycin.

effect: Potent CYP3A4 inhibition can double carbamazepine exposure, causing severe toxicity.
recommendation: Reduce carbamazepine dose and monitor levels and toxicity signs.

effect: Valproate doubles lamotrigine exposure, raising the risk of serious rash including SJS/TEN.
recommendation: Halve the lamotrigine starting dose and titrate slowly when valproate is present.

effect: Phenytoin accelerates T4/T3 metabolism and displacement, increasing levothyroxine requirement.
recommendation: Monitor TSH 6-8 weeks after starting phenytoin; adjust levothyroxine dose.

effect: CYP2C9/2D6 inhibition can raise phenytoin to toxic levels.
recommendation: Monitor phenytoin levels closely and reduce dose if toxicity signs appear.

effect: Potassium supplementation with a potassium-sparing diuretic risks severe hyperkalemia.
recommendation: Avoid routine K+ supplements; monitor serum potassium regularly.

effect: ACE inhibition plus potassium load can cause life-threatening hyperkalemia.
recommendation: Avoid supplementation unless documented deficiency; monitor potassium.

effect: ARB plus potassium supplementation raises hyperkalemia and arrhythmia risk.
recommendation: Monitor serum potassium; avoid routine supplements.

effect: Trimethoprim potassium-sparing effect plus spironolactone causes hyperkalemia.
recommendation: Monitor potassium closely during TMP-SMX in patients on spironolactone.

effect: TMP-SMX plus ACE inhibition raises the risk of significant hyperkalemia.
recommendation: Check potassium at baseline and 3-5 days after starting TMP-SMX.

effect: Dual potassium retention markedly increases hyperkalemia risk.
recommendation: Avoid combination or monitor potassium very closely.

effect: Potassium-sparing diuretic plus ACE inhibitor can cause dangerous hyperkalemia.
recommendation: Monitor serum potassium and creatinine regularly.

effect: Iron-ciprofloxacin chelation markedly reduces antibiotic absorption and efficacy.
recommendation: Give ciprofloxacin 2 hours before or 6 hours after iron supplementation.

effect: Iron chelates tetracyclines, reducing both antibiotic and iron absorption.
recommendation: Separate by at least 3 hours; take iron at a different time of day.

effect: Iron reduces levothyroxine absorption, raising TSH over time.
recommendation: Separate by at least 4 hours; recheck TSH after starting iron.

effect: Antacids reduce mycophenolate mofetil absorption by up to a third.
recommendation: Separate doses by at least 2 hours and monitor for rejection risk.

effect: Sucralfate binds phenytoin in the gut, reducing absorption and serum levels.
recommendation: Administer sucralfate 2 hours before or 6 hours after phenytoin.

effect: Polyvalent cations chelate raltegravir, lowering antiviral exposure.
recommendation: Separate by at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after raltegravir.

effect: Calcium-tetracycline chelation impairs absorption of both agents.
recommendation: Space administration by 2-3 hours; prefer doxycycline if calcium is required.

effect: Cimetidine inhibits warfarin metabolism, modestly raising INR and bleeding risk.
recommendation: Monitor INR when starting/stopping cimetidine; consider famotidine instead.

effect: Cimetidine reduces theophylline clearance, risking toxicity.
recommendation: Monitor theophylline levels or switch to famotidine.

effect: Cimetidine inhibits metformin renal tubular secretion, raising metformin levels.
recommendation: Monitor for GI intolerance; consider an H2 blocker with less interaction.

effect: Prolonged PPI therapy can raise phenytoin levels via CYP2C19 inhibition.
recommendation: Monitor phenytoin levels during prolonged PPI use.

effect: Disulfiram-like reaction with flushing, vomiting, tachycardia, and hypotension.
recommendation: Counsel complete alcohol abstinence during and 48-72 hours after therapy.

effect: Xanthine oxidase inhibition blocks azathioprine clearance, causing severe myelosuppression.
recommendation: Contraindicated. Reduce azathioprine to 25% if combination is unavoidable.

effect: Xanthine oxidase inhibition massively increases 6-MP exposure, causing fatal pancytopenia.
recommendation: Contraindicated; reduce 6-MP dose to 25% or use alternative urate-lowering drug.

effect: Macrolide inhibition of ergotamine metabolism causes severe vasospasm and ischemia.
recommendation: Contraindicated; use a non-interacting antibiotic.

effect: Strong CYP3A4 inhibition produces ergotism with ischemic limb and CNS complications.
recommendation: Contraindicated within 72 hours of clarithromycin or any strong 3A4 inhibitor.

effect: Combined nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity risk is substantially higher than either agent alone.
recommendation: Monitor renal function and drug levels closely; avoid prolonged overlap.

effect: Loop diuretics add ototoxicity and can worsen aminoglycoside-induced hearing loss.
recommendation: Monitor audiometry and renal function; consider an alternative diuretic.

effect: Enzyme induction accelerates steroid metabolism, risking adrenal crisis on stress.
recommendation: Increase steroid dose empirically and counsel on sick-day rules.

effect: Bidirectional CYP interactions raise carbamazepine-epoxide levels and alter valproate metabolism.
recommendation: Monitor levels of both drugs; watch for ataxia or sedation.

effect: Metoclopramide blocks central dopamine receptors, worsening parkinsonian symptoms.
recommendation: Avoid metoclopramide in Parkinson disease; use an alternative prokinetic.

effect: CYP2D6 inhibition reduces conversion of tamoxifen to its active metabolite endoxifen.
recommendation: Prefer SSRIs with weak CYP2D6 effects such as citalopram or escitalopram.

effect: CYP2D6 inhibition lowers endoxifen formation, reducing tamoxifen efficacy.
recommendation: Choose an alternative antidepressant with less CYP2D6 inhibition.
